title: The Belfort syllabus
promise: Practical skills for swing and positional trading in Indian cash equities: how to read a chart, size a trade, check a business, keep a journal and stay out of scams. Nothing you do not need to make a decision this week.
screening_test: Decision test: does this topic change a decision a cash-market swing or positional trader makes in a normal week (what to study, where to enter, where the stop goes, how much to buy, when to exit)? If not, it is out.
Evidence test: is there measurable evidence it helps, or can Belfort show the evidence? Folklore is taught only as 'what people believe and what the data says'.
Practice test: can the learner try it inside Belfort within five minutes (replay, paper trade, prediction, research report)? Every lesson ends with something to do.
Safety test: does knowing it protect the learner's money or rights (costs, taxes, scams, regulation)? Safety topics pass even when they are not about trading decisions.
Order test: is everything it depends on taught earlier? Lessons build in one direction.

skipped.why: Leverage beginners cannot afford. SEBI's own studies found most individual F&O traders lose money. Out of scope until a later, clearly separated advanced track.
Needs live data and fast execution that Belfort does not provide, and is where costs hurt beginners most.

skipped.topic: Discounted cash flow models, CAPM, beta theory
skipped.why: Valuation theory for analysts. A trader needs P/E against peers, debt and growth, which the business module teaches.

skipped.topic: Efficient market theory and academic portfolio theory
skipped.why: Interesting, but changes no weekly decision. Its useful core (diversify, size small) is taught in Risk and Portfolio.
Traders need five numbers from the statements and their red flags, not Ind AS detail.
No reliable evidence. Mentioned once in Scams and myths so learners recognise them.
Different markets and rules. Out of scope.
